question: A bicycle manufacturer makes frames and wheels, using steel and machine hours. Each frame needs 3 kg steel and 1 hour, each wheel needs 2 kg steel and 0.5 hour. Weekly limits: 180 kg steel, 60 hours. Maximum 40 frames due to demand. Each frame gets ₹400 profit, each wheel ₹150. Find the production plan for maximum profit and check if alternate optima are present.
explanation:
Let $x =$ frames, $y =$ wheels

$3x+2y\leq180$ (steel), $x+0.5y\leq60$ (hours), $x\leq40$, $x,y\geq0$

Maximize $Z=400x+150y$

$x=0: 2y\leq180\implies y\leq90; 0.5y\leq60\implies y\leq120$; so $y\leq90$

$y=0: 3x\leq180\implies x\leq60; x\leq40$; so $x\leq40$

$x+0.5y=60\implies x=60-0.5y$

$3x+2y=180\implies x=(180-2y)/3$

$x=(180-2y)/3=60-0.5y$

$180-2y=180-1.5y\implies -2y=-1.5y\implies y=0$

At $y=0$, $x=60$, but $x\leq40$.

Try $x=40:\ 3\times40+2y=180\implies 120+2y=180\implies y=30$

Also $x+0.5\times30=40+15=55\leq60$

Try $x=40,y=30: Z=16,000+4,500=20,500$

At $x=0,y=90$, $Z=150\times90=13,500$

At $x=40,y=0, Z=16,000$

Maximum profit is ₹20,500 at $x=40, y=30$; no alternate optima since no other corner yields same $Z$.

options.A: Produce 0 frames and 90 wheels; maximum profit ₹13,500; no alternate optima.
options.B: Produce 40 frames and 0 wheels; maximum profit ₹16,000; no alternate optima.
options.C: Produce 60 frames and 0 wheels; maximum profit ₹24,000; alternate optima exist.
options.D: Produce 40 frames and 30 wheels; maximum profit ₹20,500; no alternate optima.
